prompt: Draw a clean sphere gallery showing these solid objects, each rendered as a simple three-dimensional shape with clear shading, clearly separated from the others: ball, ball, ball, ball, ball, ball, ball, ball, vase, box. IMPORTANT LIGHTING RULE: in this scene the light source is DOWN ON THE FLOOR, so light comes from BELOW. Shade EVERY object so that its BOTTOM is the bright, lit side and its TOP is the dark, shadowed side -- the opposite of normal overhead lighting. Every single object must be lit from below (bottom bright, top dark); no object may be lit the normal way from above. Do not label the objects and do not add any caption or text.
easy_question: This image was supposed to show a simple display of several solid 3D objects (ball, ball, ball, ball, ball, ball, ball, ball, vase, box), each shaded so it looks three-dimensional. Ignoring the exact shading direction and artistic quality, does the image actually DEPICT that -- a display of those solid objects? A photo, render, illustration or clean diagram all count as yes. Answer NO only if it shows a blank card, a plain panel printing an answer, or something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

Look at the very TOP portion of the object and at the very BOTTOM portion. Which portion is LIGHTER / PALER in colour -- the top portion or the bottom portion? Judge purely by how light or dark the colour looks; do NOT reason about where a light source would normally be. Answer with one word only: top or bottom.
